title: Romance
identity: The catalog’s alto saxophone/piano edition is Marc Reift EMR2296E, as identified by retailer search results. The attribution to Carl Maria von Weber is highly doubtful: Weber died in 1826, while the work first appeared in 1890 for euphonium, an instrument developed later; the scholarly Weber edition retains it only among doubtful attributions.

evidence.claim: Scholarly Weber-Gesamtausgabe research reports the first known publication in 1890 for euphonium and concludes Weber authorship is highly improbable; later editions appeared for cello, bassoon, trombone, and viola.
evidence.source_name: Carl-Maria-von-Weber-Gesamtausgabe, “Die Romanza appassionata – eine Komposition von Weber?”

evidence.claim: Retail listing identifies Marc Reift EMR2296E for alto saxophone and piano; the product page itself is not opened.

Scholarly source explains that this piece first appeared in 1890 for euphonium, after Weber’s death, and argues the attribution is highly improbable; it remains under doubtful attribution in the Weber catalogue.

review_focus: Inference: confirm that the saxophone edition derives from the same late-19th-century Romanza appassionata before judging its musical demands; Weber attribution should not be treated as settled.
collection_flag: Later saxophone arrangement of a work with doubtful Weber attribution. Historical identity and saxophone score require confirmation.
gaps: Exact author and source version remain uncertain.
No saxophone score, recording, or programming evidence was verified.
